land.text: Austria, annexed to Germany in 1938; on 27 April 1945 the Declaration of Independence 'declared Austria's secession from the Third Reich'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Republic of Austria row (slug republic-of-austria) ends in 1937; the 1938-1945 interval is inside Nazi Germany. The pages opened do not date the 1938 Anschluss.

capitals.name: Vienna
capitals.note: Capital throughout; 'Vienna was divided among all four Allies' in 1945-1955 (Allied-occupied Austria page) but remained the seat of Renner's provisional government.

correction.text: the whole country as in Cliopatria's 1947 shape: the four occupation zones together cover Salzburg, Upper Austria, Carinthia, Styria, East Tyrol, Tyrol, Vorarlberg, Burgenland, Lower Austria and Vienna

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first shape is 1946 but the page gives 'Established: 27 April 1945' and the 9 July 1945 agreement that divided the whole of Austria into four zones. The Allied Council 'refused to recognize Renner's claim of a national government' until the Western allies recognised his reformed cabinet on 20 October 1945, so 1945 is drawn as the whole country under occupation (hatched by zone, ledger).

correction.text: the whole country: the 1946 shape (59,811 km2) omits the Soviet zone, which the 1947 shape (85,349 km2) restores; the gazetteer measures the difference at about 25,800 km2 (Lower Austria, Burgenland, Vienna and the Mühlviertel)

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1946 shape stops at the western zones; the page puts 'Burgenland, Lower Austria, and the Mühlviertel area of Upper Austria' in the Soviet zone of the same state and says the Allies 'signed the Second Control Agreement' on 28 June 1946, loosening their control over the government. One state, four zones: use the 1947 outline for 1946 and hatch the zones. Infobox area (Austria page) 83,879 km2 versus 85,349 km2 in 1947 (ratio 1.02).

85,349 km2 against the Austria infobox's 83,879 km2 (ratio 1.02, well inside a factor of two). Nothing in the pages opened moves Austria's frontier between 1947 and 2024 ('None are stated'); the 1947-1991 outline is the modern frontier. Carinthia was held against Yugoslav demands (State Treaty page, undated).

85,056 km2 against the infobox's 83,879 km2 (ratio 1.01). The 293 km2 difference from 1947 is Cliopatria's change of source outline, not a boundary event: no page opened reports a border change in 1992.
Same outline as 1992 (85,056 km2); the state is alive in 2024 (EU member since 1 January 1995, per the Austria page).

region.text: "Yugoslav troops occupied parts of Carinthia, including the capital city of Klagenfurt"

ledger.note: 1945: Yugoslav troops occupy parts of Carinthia including Klagenfurt at the end of the Second World War. The page gives no month and says the Allies did not reach Carinthia before 8 May 1945; the radius is the researcher's reading of 'parts of Carinthia'. The troops are those of the Yugoslav Army, before the federal republic's constitution of 1946; counterpart is the Yugoslav state of May 1945 (slug yugoslavia), since the Federal People's Republic was proclaimed only on 29 November 1945 (SFRY page; reviewer eu-22-b).

region.text: the Carinthian land the Yugoslavs held

ledger.note: 1945: the Yugoslavs withdraw from Carinthia, 'soon forced to withdraw by the British forces'. The page gives no date; 1945 is the researcher's reading of 'soon' after the end of the war (confidence 2).

region.text: Austria, whose provisional government under Karl Renner took office on 27 April 1945

ledger.note: 1945: Renner's provisional government takes office in Vienna and the Second Republic dates from 27 April. 'Seven days later Renner's cabinet took office' after the Soviets 'instructed Renner to form a provisional government' on 20 April; infobox 'Established: 27 April 1945'. The Austria page: the Declaration of Independence 'declared Austria's secession from the Third Reich'. The pages give the government, not a boundary: the country is drawn whole (confidence 2).

region.text: "Salzburg and Upper Austria south of the Danube were assigned to the American Zone."

ledger.note: 1945: the American zone, Salzburg and Upper Austria south of the Danube. 'On 9 July 1945 the Allies agreed on the borders of their occupation zones'; troop movements ('zone swap') continued to the end of July and the first Americans reached Vienna at the end of July.

region.text: "East Tyrol, Carinthia, and Styria were assigned to the British Zone."

ledger.note: 1945: the British zone, East Tyrol, Carinthia and Styria, from the 9 July 1945 agreement on the zones; the British arrived in Vienna in September (page: no day).

region.text: "Vorarlberg and North Tyrol were assigned to the French Zone." (North Tyrol is the Tyrol state without East Tyrol, which went to the British zone)

ledger.note: 1945: the French zone, Vorarlberg and North Tyrol, from the 9 July 1945 agreement on the zones.

region.text: "Burgenland, Lower Austria, and the Mühlviertel area of Upper Austria" were assigned to the Soviet zone; Vienna, divided among all four Allies, lies inside it

ledger.note: 1945: the Soviet zone, Burgenland, Lower Austria and the Mühlviertel, from the 9 July 1945 agreement on the zones. 'Vienna was divided among all four Allies' with an international zone in the old centre and the guard changing monthly; the page gives no district list, so Vienna is drawn with the surrounding Soviet zone.

region.text: "Salzburg and Upper Austria south of the Danube were assigned to the American Zone."

ledger.note: 1955: the American zone is free of occupation. The State Treaty was signed on 15 May and came into force on 27 July 1955 and 'on 25 October the country was free of occupying troops'; the neutrality law followed on 26 October (Austria page).

region.text: "East Tyrol, Carinthia, and Styria were assigned to the British Zone."

ledger.note: 1955: the British zone is free of occupation, 'on 25 October the country was free of occupying troops'.

region.text: "Vorarlberg and North Tyrol were assigned to the French Zone." (North Tyrol is the Tyrol state without East Tyrol, which went to the British zone)

ledger.note: 1955: the French zone is free of occupation, 'on 25 October the country was free of occupying troops'. The French Fourth Republic's Cliopatria row ends in 1957, the Fifth Republic from 1958.

region.text: "Burgenland, Lower Austria, and the Mühlviertel area of Upper Austria" were assigned to the Soviet zone; Vienna, divided among all four Allies, lies inside it

ledger.note: 1955: the Soviet zone and Vienna are free of occupation, 'on 25 October the country was free of occupying troops'. The Austrian State Treaty page agrees: 'the Allies left Austrian territory on 25 October 1955'.

wars.name: Yugoslav occupation of Carinthia (1945)
wars.outcome: The Yugoslav troops were 'soon forced to withdraw by the British forces'; Carinthia, East Tyrol and Styria formed the British zone and Austria 'successfully held its part of Carinthia against the demands of a resurgent Federal People's Republic of Yugoslavia' (State Treaty page, undated).
wars.note: A standoff at the end of the Second World War, not a declared war; the page names no battle and no month. Austria's other border questions (South Tyrol 'not addressed' in the State Treaty) moved no frontier.

certainty.note: Carinthia: Yugoslav and British troops held lines that no page describes; the zones themselves were agreed on 9 July 1945.

The frontier is the modern Austrian one throughout (no page opened reports a change); the pages opened do not quote the State Treaty's frontier clause, so the sharpness rests on the unchanged outline.

notes: Austria is a single state in every year of the row; Cliopatria's 1946 shape drops the Soviet zone (Lower Austria, Burgenland, the Mühlviertel and Vienna, about 25,800 km2 by the gazetteer) and is corrected to the 1947 outline. A new keyframe for 1945 covers the months between Renner's government (27 April 1945) and Cliopatria's first shape. Occupation is modelled as hatched zones with each occupying power as counterpart (the Allied-occupied Germany convention); the matching occupation events of the four occupiers belong to their own dossiers. Yugoslav occupation of Carinthia in 1945 rests on the Carinthia article only (no month, no withdrawal date); a gap-filler could open 'World War II in the Slovene Lands' or 'Yugoslav claims on Carinthia'. The State Treaty's frontier clause (frontiers of 1 January 1938) and the 1938 Anschluss date are not on the pages opened. The cliopatria 'Republic of Austria' row (1919-1937, slug republic-of-austria) is the First Republic: a different state with a separate dossier, not merged here. Gazetteer names needed: region 'Mühlviertel' (Upper Austria north of the Danube) and 'East Tyrol' (Osttirol, the Lienz district of Tyrol). Austria is drawn alive to 2024; EU membership (1 January 1995) is an association, not territory, and Cliopatria draws no change.
